title: Riemannian or Lorentzian?
promptMarkdown: In under 250 words and without the notes open: suppose the positive definiteness in the definition of a Riemannian metric is replaced by non-degeneracy with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ (a Lorentzian metric on a 4-manifold). Name the signature convention you are using. Then say (a) which constructions and statements of this unit remain valid word for word (think of coefficients $g_{ij}$, the transformation law, the determinant, the inverse $g^{ij}$), (b) which fail or must be modified (think of arc length $\int\sqrt{g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)}$, the distance function of Proposition 5.10, and the existence proof of Theorem 5.16 via partitions of unity), giving one sentence of reason for each, and (c) why this course keeps the two cases in separate units rather than treating them together.
hintLadder: Which statements used only that $(g_{ij})$ is an invertible symmetric matrix, and which used that $g(v,v)>0$ for $v\neq0$?
Is a convex combination of two non-degenerate indefinite forms always non-degenerate? Try $\mathrm{diag}(-1,1)$ and $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$.

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies that components, the transformation law, the determinant law and the inverse metric survive (non-degeneracy is what they need).

levels.label: met
levels.description: Correct with the reason (only invertibility used).

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies that arc length needs |g(γ̇,γ̇)| or a causal restriction, that the distance function (Proposition 5.10) fails, and that the convex-combination existence proof fails (convex combinations of indefinite forms can degenerate), each with a reason.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Two of three, or reasons missing.

criteria.criterion: Signature convention named explicitly and a sensible reason for separating the cases given (different theorems, different hypotheses; avoiding silent convention switches).

difficulty.basis: No computation; the learner sorts the unit's constructions by whether they use only invertibility or positive definiteness, and gives one reason for each failure.

progression.transferNote: Compared with MAT-262-u01-ex2, where every statement is used under positive definiteness, the learner carries the unit's constructions into a setting the unit never computes in, an indefinite metric of signature (−,+,+,+), and decides for each whether it needs invertibility only or positivity. The degenerate convex combination and the collapse of the distance function are new phenomena, not new numbers.
